title: Evaluating retrieval quality for long conversations

chunks.text: How would you evaluate retrieval quality in long conversations if the goal is to make answers more reliable without changing the generation model?
I should answer with evaluation criteria, mention recall drift over long threads, and keep the framing practical for a local search tool.

Evaluating retrieval quality for long conversations starts with recall@k on known answer-bearing turns, then checks whether the reranked list still preserves chronology. For reducing hallucinations without using a larger model, the best lever is usually better evidence selection: make sure the retrieved chunks carry enough surrounding context, measure false positives on adjacent but irrelevant turns, and compare whether answer quality improves when you attach neighboring turns to the prompt.
